decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate unchanged at 1-1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Oil price premiums and other aspects of geopolitical risks have reportedly fostered continued restraint on spending and hiring by businesses.
changes.explanation: The Fed added this language to explicitly acknowledge that rising oil prices and geopolitical tensions are causing businesses to hold back on spending and hiring.

changes.quote: However, the Committee believes that as those risks lift, as most analysts expect, the accommodative stance of monetary policy, coupled with ongoing growth in productivity, will provide support to an improving economic climate over time.
changes.explanation: The Committee notes that once these temporary risks fade, low interest rates and worker productivity will help the economy improve.

tone_quotes.quote: Oil price premiums and other aspects of geopolitical risks have reportedly fostered continued restraint on spending and hiring by businesses.

In these circumstances, the Committee believes that, against the background of its long-run goals of price stability and sustainable economic growth and of the information currently available, the risks are balanced with respect to the prospects for both goals for the foreseeable future.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 13.36% APR costs about $55.67 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.06% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 5.97% would rise by about $11.57 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 6%, and employers added an average of -12k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.5% over the past year (December 2002); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed is keeping interest rates steady while watching how geopolitical risks and oil prices develop. It suggests future moves will depend on when those temporary restraints lift.
